Flop (Ts 8s 3c): hero checks, villain bets 3 (9-high air, IP). Hero calls with top pair.

River (Jc): hero checks, villain checks back.

Flop: Td 8s 6h. Hero checks. Villain bets 3 (into pot of ~4). Hero folds Qd7d.
Villain held 5h4c — open-ended straight draw (needs 7 for 4-5-6-7-8, or needs 3 for... actually 4-5 with 6-8-T: 4-5-6-7-8 needs 7 = OESD).
Result: villain wins small pot with semi-bluff on draw.
Key observations:
1. Limp range now includes OFFSUIT connectors (5h4c) not just suited — range is very wide.
2. Another IP flop bet with draw equity (5th IP flop bet, 5/5).
3. Hero folded a hand that had 7-high (poor) but could have been a gutshot with Q-T-8-6 needing 9.

nodes.title: Hand 29 — Villain limps SB with 8s9c, raises flop+turn as OESD bluff, hero wins with AA
nodes.body:
Hero BB: AcAs. Villain SB limps (8s9c — offsuit connector, fits limp range).
Hero 3-bets to 16, villain calls.
Flop: 4h 5d 3c — villain has OESD (needs 6 or 7 for straight). Hero bets 22, villain RAISES to 124, hero calls.
Turn: 7h — board now 3-4-5-7. Villain still drawing (needs 6 for 5-6-7-8-9 or 3-4-5-6-7). Hero bets 22, villain RAISES again (~98 more). Action ends (all-in or last street).
River: Tc — villain's draw bricks. Showdown: villain 8s9c (high card) vs hero AcAs (one pair). Hero wins +162.

KEY FINDING: Villain went TWO streets of aggressive raising with a pure draw (OESD), never hit, and lost. This CONTRADICTS the one_barrel_give_up pattern — when IP, villain is capable of multi-barreling with draws, not just one-and-done. Limp with 8s9c further confirms wide offsuit connector limp range.

Villain holds Kc5s — king-high with a gutshot (needs 3 or 7 on 4-6-Q board for 3-4-5-6 or 4-5-6-7). This is a gutshot semi-bluff / thin air c-bet IP.

Key notes:
- Another confirmed SB limp with a weak/speculative hand (Kc5s offsuit — weak king + low card). 9th limp in 16 SB opportunities.
- Another confirmed 100% IP flop c-bet — now 8/8 hands where villain was IP on flop. Board Q-6-4 with K-high, villain bets immediately.
- Hero FOLDED middle pair (66) — this was a mistake. Given villain's 100% IP c-bet rate with wide air/draw range, hero should have called middle pair here. Villain had minimal equity (gutshot only ~9%).
- Villain's limp range: now confirmed to include weak kings with low cards (Kd5h h23, Kc5s h31).

nodes.title: villain
nodes.body:
Session started 2026-06-04. 80 hands observed.

**Preflop SB strategy (45 opportunities as SB):** Fold h1,h51,h57,h67 (4 hands); limp h3,h7,h15,h17,h23,h25,h27,h29,h31,h33,h39,h43,h45,h49,h53,h55,h59,h63,h65,h69,h71,h73,h79 (23 hands); raise 4x h5,h9,h11,h13,h19,h21,h35,h37,h41,h47,h61,h75,h77 (13 hands). ~29% raise (13/45), ~51% limp (23/45), ~9% fold (4/45). Raise range: broadway+ (AKs x1, AKo x2, QJ+, QTo) AND medium/big pocket pairs (TT, JJ) AND aces broadly (A4o, A6o, A7o, A9s, AJo). Limp range: ANY connector/1-gapper (suited or offsuit) AND weak kings AND weak aces AND any offsuit weak hand AND small pocket pairs (33 confirmed) — EXTREMELY WIDE.

**BB holdings observed (38 samples, h80: 9h8d):** Range is 100% — villain defends BB with any two cards.

**Postflop — positionally aggressive; strength of hand determines multi-barrel vs. give-up:**
- IP with air (no equity): fires ONE flop barrel, gives up on turn if called.
- IP with draw (OESD/flush/gutshot): fires MULTIPLE barrels aggressively.
- IP with made hand (value, including bottom pair): bets flop and beyond.
- OOP: usually checks air through; WILL bet flop OOP occasionally (h79: bet flop OOP, folded to check-raise). Folds to check-raise OOP: 1/1.
- IP flop aggression count: 21/21 — 100% c-bet rate IP (air, draws, AND made hands including bottom pair).

**KEY EXPLOITS:**
1. SB raise range includes ANY ace and strong broadways broadly; limp range is near-any-two. Hero should 3-bet QQ+/AK vs villain SB raise.
2. IP bets are 100% (21/21). Air bluffs are one-and-done; draws are multi-street; even bottom pair gets bet. Hero should call/raise flop with middle pair+ and strong draws.
3. NEW (h79): Villain folds to check-raise OOP on flop. Check-raise OOP is a strong counter when villain bets into hero BB.
4. Hero continues to over-fold to single IP bets (folded top pair h71, gutshot+pair h73).

nodes.title: Bets flop IP with air, draws, AND made hands — 100% IP flop bet rate
nodes.body: IP flop bet count: 21/21 (100%). Includes air bluffs, OESD/flush draws, bottom pair, top pair, sets, full houses. Completely polarized by hand strength only on later streets.

nodes.title: Checks flop with weak/bottom pair
nodes.body: Villain checked flop with bottom pair (6d 4c on 4h Th Ad — flopped pair of 4s). Did not c-bet or donk. Slow-play or uncertainty with weak made hands. Occurrences: 1.

nodes.title: Folds to check-raise OOP on flop
nodes.body: Hand 79: Villain bet flop OOP (3c-3d-Js), hero check-raised, villain folded. First observed instance. Villain may over-fold to aggression when OOP. Count: 1/1 folds to flop check-raise OOP.

nodes.title: Multi-barrels (raise flop + raise turn) with strong draws IP
nodes.body:
Villain is capable of firing multiple streets of aggression with draws, not just one barrel.
Hand 29: limped SB with 8s9c, called 3-bet. Flop 4h-5d-3c gave OESD — villain RAISED hero's flop bet. Turn 7h (still drawing to 6) — villain RAISED hero's turn bet again. Draw bricked on Tc river. Pure draw, two aggressive raises, never made hand.
Contrast with hand 15 (gave up on turn after flop bluff called with pure air). The key distinction may be EQUITY: when villain has a real draw he continues multiple streets; when he has total air he gives up after one barrel.
Occurrences: 1 (hand 29).
Implication: Do NOT assume one call folds out a drawing villain. With OESD/flush draws, villain will continue aggressively. However, hero's AA held — calling down is still correct, villain's draws are often unimproved.

nodes.title: One-barrel IP bluff — gives up on turn when called and has NO draw equity
nodes.body:
When villain fires a flop bluff IP with pure air (no draw) and gets called, he shuts down on the turn.
Hand 15: bet flop with 9-high (backdoor spade draw) on Ts 8s 3c, called by hero; turn Kh — checked back; river Jc — checked back. Showdown showed pure air.
Occurrences: 1.
IMPORTANT REFINEMENT (hand 29): When villain has a real draw (OESD, flush draw), he does NOT give up — he raises multiple streets (see multi_barrel_draw tendency). The one-barrel pattern applies specifically to TOTAL AIR with no real equity. Distinguish: air = give up, draw = fire multiple barrels.

nodes.title: OOP postflop: passive with air, but does bet some hands OOP
nodes.body: Hand 7: Villain SB (OOP) with 9s7d on Qs-Kd-8s-Qd — checked flop and turn with no pair. Hand 79: Villain SB (OOP) bet flop on 3c-3d-Js, then folded to check-raise. So villain DOES bet OOP sometimes (not pure check-air). Pattern is bluffs/bets more aggressively IP, but will fire at least one flop bet OOP too. Villain folds to check-raise OOP: 1/1.

nodes.title: Folds SB preflop vs BB
nodes.body: Hero folds SB preflop, villain BB holdings revealed: ATo (h4), K7o (h6), As8c (h8), AdTc (h10), AsTs (h12), Ks3d (h14), 3s6h (h16), 3s6c (h18), 7s6h (h20), 2h5c (h22), 7dKs (h24), Ad5s (h26), 9cJh (h28), 8d2d (h30), 4cQh (h32), Kd9h (h34), 8dJd (h36), 5h2s (h38), 4h7s (h40), 6cKc (h42), 9d6h (h44), 2s7c (h46), Ah4d (h50). 23 BB instances. Villain's BB range is 100% — defends with any two cards.\n\nVillain SB FOLDS: h1 (trash), h51 (unknown), h57 (unknown). 3 SB folds in ~31 SB opportunities. Still extremely rare; villain almost never folds SB.

nodes.title: Limps SB preflop with speculative / marginal hands
nodes.body: Limps SB 19/35 opportunities (~54%). Range is extremely wide: any connector, 1-gapper (suited or offsuit), weak kings, weak aces, random offsuit junk (Js4c, 2cTc, Jh7c, 3h4d), AND small pocket pairs (3c3h confirmed h53). Hands: h3,h7,h15,h17,h23,h25,h27,h29,h31,h33,h39,h43,h45,h49,h53,h55,h59,h63,h65.

nodes.title: Raises SB preflop vs BB
nodes.body: Raises 4x from SB: AKs (h5), QJo (h9), QdJd (h11), TdQc (h13), TdTh (h19), Ad4s (h21), AcKs (h35), Ad6c (h37), JsJd (h41), Ac9c (h47), As7c (h61), AsJd (h75). 12/41 SB opportunities = ~29%. Range includes premium broadway, medium/big pocket pairs (TT, JJ), weak aces (A4o, A6o, A7o), suited aces (A9s), AND AJo. Raise range is wide — any ace, strong broadway, pairs TT+. Hero should 3-bet/call wide vs this range.

nodes.title: Calls river bet with solid made hand (two pair+)
nodes.body: Hand 7: Villain called hero's river bet of 2 (into ~6 pot) holding two pair (9s7d, board Qs Kd 8s Qd 9d = 9s + paired Qs). Comfortable calling with non-nut but strong made hands on the river. River calls: 1.

nodes.title: Checks back river with one pair (pot control)
nodes.body: Villain checked river after betting turn, holding one pair (bottom pair). Went to showdown passively — pot control / thin value avoidance with marginal holdings. Occurrences: 1.

nodes.title: Bets turn with weak pair after checking flop
nodes.body: Villain checked flop then bet turn (3 into ~6) with bottom pair on a coordinated board (4h Th Ad 3h). Delayed aggression — may use turn as first bet with medium-strength hands. Occurrences: 1.
